Lionheart Fixt 0.10.1 - what has happened since the thieves' guild

The last post here was 0.5.1, the thieves' guild. Ten releases have gone out since, and
I have not been keeping the thread current, so this is the catch-up. Everything below is
in the current download. Latest: 0.10.1.

Fixt is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt. It
fixes what is broken, restores what was cut, and adds new content only where the game
plainly ran out. Every check adds a route and none removes one, so the vanilla solution
to every scene still works.

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases


0.6.0 - the Port District: the fourth companion

Lionheart ships with three companions. It was written with four. Fernand Desoto, the
sailor who asks you to save his brother, has 31 dialogue nodes and 17 of them could not
be reached - the entire success branch, including a real "join the party" action and a
14KB relay on the map waiting to give him companion banter. None of it could happen
because Juan could not be saved: the trigger on his body declared him dead no matter
what, and the quest shipped with two states, neither a success.

Now Juan is dying, not dead, when you reach him - about forty-five seconds, with the
vodyanoi usually still coming - and the healing potion Fernand presses on you is for
him. Save him and he walks back to his brother, Fernand tells him off for fishing off
the north island alone (three new lines; the rest is the game's own), and Fernand can
come with you. Miss the clock and the quest falls back to the ending the game already
had. Also: the Duke's murder leaves a crime scene with two guards holding it, the fish
monger buys skulls without dropping the conversation, and there is a reward for selling
him a great many of them.


0.7.0 - the road north: the Knights of Saladin get a career

Amir's speech sending you to Montserrat says "I shall mark the path on your map" and
contained no map-marking action. That one missing line is why the Knights of Saladin
led nowhere. Fixed, and the order now has the three ranks that were written and costed
(Aswaran, Blessed, Exalted - the largest melee progression in the game, and Turn Undead
at the top). Amir attends the Cathedral summit himself instead of Javier reading his
report in the third person; the summit's three deleted relays are rebuilt, which also
fixes the scene for a player who serves no order at all, who used to reach a room with
no conversation and no way out.


0.8.0 - the Gate District remainder

DaVinci's spirit-gem branch - three nodes on whether to cross the Inquisition for him,
reachable by nothing. Weng Choi's "most valued customer" greeting, guarded by a
conditional whose both outcomes opened the same node. Merchant Lope's Perception haggle,
offered from nowhere. The goblin sapper's name. Two people who greeted you as a stranger
forever. And the district's 42 orphaned replies read one by one and accounted for: none
of them is a cut quest. There is no further list.


0.8.1 to 0.8.4 - what the first playthrough found

Fernand's draught could eat whatever potion you happened to carry. Quinn's reagent
errands could be started twice and turned in with too few reagents. The lava trolls'
peace had a two-second race that left one hostile. Amir would not give a Favored One
his directions on the greeting he actually uses. The fish monger did not count bartered
skulls. Each fixed on its own branch with nothing else in it.


0.9.0 - the Temple District, and the first step into Act 3

Refuse Machiavelli in Barcelona and he threatens to seek aid "from those that seek to
do us harm." Save him and he promises to repay you in Montaillou. Both endings written,
and he is on no Montaillou map. He is at the inn now: refuse him and the Old Man's
assassins come in behind him; save him and he pays. Na Roqua greets a friend of the
Cathars as one, on two voiced lines nothing reached, and tells you where the thing that
can kill the daeva is kept. Torquemada acknowledges his own Inquisitor for the Khan.
Read and deliberately left alone: Torquemada's second task, purify the shadow dryad -
she is Na Roqua, she has ten thousand hit points, and attacking her throws you out of
her house. Unfinished, not cut.


0.9.1 to 0.9.4 - around Barcelona, and a crash I shipped

The Mongol Camp's gate guard greets a welcomed player instead of falling silent for the
rest of the game. Brendan the Irish sailor hands over the clover from drowned Ireland -
a line, an icon and a Luck check the game shipped and never connected. Then the repairs:
Juan as a dying man rather than a corpse (so the spirit skills cannot drain him and
soft-lock the rescue), the Vodyanoi Anatomist perk actually doing something for the
first time, the Saladin summit playing to its end, the troll chief handing over a hide
to the player who made peace with him.

And 0.9.4 is a hotfix you should have: 0.9.1's gate greeting carried one value led by
stray tabs, and the engine refused the whole map rather than the line. Entering the
Mongol Camp on 0.9.1 through 0.9.3 could stop the game. Fixed, and the build check now
catches that class of mistake.


0.10.0 - Montserrat

This is the first release whose centre is new content rather than restoration, because
Montserrat is the first place the shipped game plainly ran out: five maps, one
conversation, and sixty identical fights against eight recolours of one snake.

Now: human assassins walk with the snakebreed, and a priestess in the larger packs who
has to die first. A sentry calls two packs down on you if you wound him and live. An
ambush in the hall, a poisoned tripwire, a trapped chest; a thief finds and steps over
all of it. Sir Tomas de Vilanova, who led the Templars that never came back, lies at the
gate with his journal, and whoever sent you north will take it from you. One of the
killers among the dead is still breathing and can be questioned. Sahar, the rearguard's
captain, speaks before she fights and fights in phases - or alone, if you can convince
her you are Machiavelli's courier. And the sanctum is an abbey now, with ten things to
click between the gate and the empty reliquary that tell you what happened here. Nobody
says where the monks went.

Also in it: Quinn's earned potions appear in his ordinary shop, and the Desoto brothers'
reunion plays.


0.10.1 - the chests that turned the guild on you

Five chests in the thieves' secret stashes ran a hidden Sneak check the moment the loot
dropped. Fail it and every thief, guard dog and Juanita turned hostile, across three
maps, permanently, without a word - no line of sight, no distance, Lockpick irrelevant.
Every other stash in the game at least shouts "Thief!" first. Now these do too: a thief
shouts when you are caught, a line tells you when you were not, both go to the log, and
the guild needs a living thief on the map to raise the alarm.


Before you install

Download, unzip, run Mod Manager.bat. It installs over any earlier release and works on
any save, with the usual caveat: anything that adds people or things to a map takes
effect on a character who has not entered that map yet. Montserrat needs a character
who has never been there. Dialogue-only changes work everywhere.

Honesty about testing: 0.6.0 through 0.9.x have been played through by one person and
repaired from what that found. Most of 0.10.0's Montserrat - the boss fight's phases,
the hover trail, the build levers - is built and not yet played end to end, and the
release notes say so. If you would rather wait for a build somebody has walked all the
way through, wait for 0.10.2. If you do play it, what you find goes straight into the
next patch.

The whole thing is on GitHub under MIT, with the full account of every read - including
the ones that ended in "leave it alone" - in docs/releases.md.
